Premature

/pree-muh-CHOOR/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Premature means occurring, arriving, or done before the usual, proper, or expected time; too early.

Premature means occurring or done before the proper or expected time — too early. The fans' premature celebration turned to silence when the other team scored in the final seconds.

Worked Example

The startup's premature launch of its app left thousands of users battling crashes the developers had not yet fixed.

The launch didn't just happen early — it happened before the app was ready, before the proper time. That 'before it should have' judgment is what premature adds beyond plain 'early.'

How Premature Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

untimely

untimely: happening at a bad or wrong time, especially too soon

hasty

hasty: done with too much speed and too little preparation

early

early: before the scheduled or usual time

Antonyms

timely

timely: happening at exactly the right moment

overdue

overdue: coming later than it should have

How Strong Is It? — early → rash → premature

early vs. premature

early vs. premature: Early is weaker — it neutrally means before the scheduled time, and can even be a good thing; premature adds that the thing came before it properly should have.

rash vs. premature

rash vs. premature: Rash is stronger — it condemns the careless judgment behind an act, while premature only faults its timing.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, in advance (Latin prae-)

Root — mature

Root — mature: ripe, fully developed (Latin maturus)

Put it together

Put it together: Pre- ('before') + maturus ('ripe') builds 'ripe before its time.' Something premature arrives before it has properly ripened — like fruit picked green.

Use the root in a new word: maturation

Use the root in a new word: maturation: The cheese needs eighteen months of maturation in the cellar before it is ready to sell.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / slightly formal

Premature pairs naturally with nouns like celebration, conclusion, announcement, and judgment ('it's premature to say'). Unlike plain 'early,' it almost always implies the timing was a mistake — something happened before it properly should have. In medicine, it describes babies born before full term.
